verdicts.summary: A prompt queued before the dialog mounts is kept and shown. An expired one shows Expired plus Dismiss. Only the head request is removed.
verdicts.scenario: A prompt arrives on /pair before SshPasswordPromptDialog mounts and is already expired when the dialog mounts. I checked whether it blocks the queue or gets answered wrongly.

verdicts.summary: The Escape observer runs only when no scope or page consumed the key, which matches the old defaultPrevented skip. It is gated on the /pull-requests pathname.
verdicts.scenario: A dialog or scope handles Escape on /pull-requests, or the key is held down. I checked whether the observer still navigates back.

verdicts.summary: The probe result replaces the vscode fallback only when it is non-empty. A rejection leaves the fallback in place, as before. I did not re-open remoteOpen.ts in this session and relied on the note's description.
verdicts.scenario: The bridge probe rejects or never resolves, so the picker keeps the vscode fallback list.

verdicts.summary: I could not confirm whether reading the thread atoms before sign-in starts shell subscriptions. The migration also marks a thread as migrated before it knows the local visit data is loaded.
verdicts.scenario: On /pair or /connect, startThreadVisitedMigration subscribes immediately to threadShellsAtom (useThreadVisitedMigration.ts:37). That atom reads snapshotAtom(environmentId) for every enabled environment (threadShell.ts:378-380, 166). Whether reading snapshotAtom opens a shell subscription is decided where the web app supplies it, in apps/web/src/state/threads.ts, which I did not open. If it does, the migration can fire threadEnvironment.visit from a page that never ran it. migratedThreadKeys.add runs at line 22, before the local value is read at line 23. So if useUiStateStore has not hydrated yet, the thread is skipped and never retried.
verdicts.missing: The apps/web snapshotAtom implementation, to see whether reading it opens a connection before auth. Also whether useUiStateStore is hydrated synchronously at app start.
